clue.text: Prophet, a man honoured in an African country

indicators.note: in asks for the short pieces before it to be placed inside the name of the African country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a man honoured by the Crown

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet turns out to be a celebrated man in some African state.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a crossword staple for Companion of Honour, so 'man honoured' reads as a person but gives two letters; the container is signalled by 'in' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the last of the Old Testament minor prophets, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Hamlet called his thing a long-runner

definitions.meaning: Hamlet named his play within the play, 'the thing' to catch the King, after a trap for mice
Agatha Christie's play of that name has run in London's West End since 1952

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet gave this title to the play he staged before Claudius; Agatha Christie's whodunit of the same title is the longest-running stage show.

clue.text: Courtly friend is …

parts.note: barristers in court politely call a fellow counsel 'my ... friend', and the next clue continues the sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers address each other as 'my learned friend', and learned also means erudite.

clue.text: … far from dim (in terms of 22 dn)

definitions.text: … far from dim (in terms of 22 dn)

parts.words: … far from dim (in terms of 22 dn)
parts.note: in musical terms 'dim' is short for diminuendo, getting quieter; the opposite is a steady swelling in volume

explanation.walkthrough: Read with 2 down, 'friend is far from dim' looks like praise of intelligence; 22 down is MUSIC, so dim is the marking dim. for diminuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness, the reverse of a diminuendo.

clue.text: Where we enjoy service, but short measure

parts.note: in tells us where something is enjoyed, inside a place

indicators.note: short means the phrase is cut down, the end of its last word removed

parts.note: church can mean a service, as in 'after church'

explanation.surface: We like the church service, though the measures are mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CHURCH to CH, the usual abbreviation; the surface reads as a grumble about a mean church measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length in imperial measurement.

clue.text: Swansea neighbour is no plain speaker

definitions.meaning: a headland and village beside Swansea in South Wales
someone who speaks indistinctly, swallowing words, is not speaking plainly

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a seaside village next to Swansea; the other is the verb for talking indistinctly, as an unclear speaker does.

clue.text: Capital film !

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a chief city, the other is Fritz Lang's classic silent picture of that title.

clue.text: A long way to French Polynesia ?

definitions.meaning: Polynesia means 'many islands'; in French mille îles is 'a thousand islands', run together

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a great distance; the other is a punning French phrase for a thousand isles, which is what Polynesia's name means.

clue.text: Wool-produce loan arranged, raising nothing

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of loan are put in a new order
in a down clue raising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A loan is arranged for a wool business, with no rise in costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns LOAN into LANO; 'raising' turns NIL upwards into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the grease extracted from sheep's wool, a by-product of it.

clue.text: A cane makes us dapper

definitions.meaning: a stroke of the cane stings, making the punished sting

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to sting with pain; the other means well-dressed.

clue.text: To South Africa this custom's boloney

indicators.note: the clue says this word with South Africa added to it makes boloney, so we take that addition away again

parts.note: boloney (bologna) is a kind of sausage

explanation.surface: A traveller to South Africa dismisses a local custom as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boloney' looks like slang for nonsense but is the sausage; SA plus the answer spells SAUSAGE, so the indicator 'To' means remove SA. 'this' points at the answer and ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice or habit, the same thing as a custom.

clue.text: Naval punishment inter alia a back number in Spain

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, was the whip used for flogging in the navy

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so one piece is put inside the word alia
the word number, abbreviated, is read backwards

explanation.surface: A list of punishments, including flogging, in some Spanish naval record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter' reads as the Latin 'among' in 'inter alia', but it is the verb 'bury': ON (NO, from 'number', turned by 'back') is buried in ALIA. The lone 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is the north-eastern region of Spain around Barcelona, so a place found within that country.

clue.text: Girl had in France a place on the Riviera

parts.note: eu is the French past participle of avoir, to have, so 'had' in French
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A young woman owned a property on the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a woman's given name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Cuirass of carbon or steel construction

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: construction suggests the letters are built up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A breastplate could be made of carbon fibre or steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' reads as how the armour is made, but it signals the rearrangement, and C for carbon is the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A corselet is a piece of body armour covering the torso, as a cuirass does.

clue.text: Ron's involved in dairy produce in the Thracian peninsula

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the dairy product

parts.note: cheese is made in a dairy

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Ron's, taken without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man named Ron is involved in Balkan farm produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' looks like Ron's involvement in a business; it is the anagram signal, and 'in' the container. The second 'in' is a link. CHERSONESE is Greek for peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian Chersonese is the ancient name of the Gallipoli peninsula; chersonese is Greek for peninsula.

clue.text: Revolutionary article on defence project

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A radical writes a piece about a military defence scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' is the noun-like 'projection': a redan is a fortification that juts out.
explanation.definitionFit: A redan is a V-shaped fieldwork pointing towards the enemy, a projecting part of a line of defence.

clue.text: Deceives admiral with optical signals

parts.note: Samuel Hood was a famous British admiral
winks are signals made with the eye

explanation.surface: An admiral misleads the enemy using visual signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink someone is to trick or fool them.

clue.text: Point a writer has to accept to make a hundred

parts.note: W, west, is a compass point
a pen is a writing instrument
to take is to accept

explanation.surface: An essayist must accept a point to score a century.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundred here is an old English county subdivision, not a number; the wapentake was its equivalent in the Danelaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A wapentake was a division of a shire in northern England, the counterpart of a hundred elsewhere.

clue.text: No night-light in bed

parts.note: the daytime source of light, found growing in a garden flower bed rather than a bedroom

explanation.definitionFit: A sunflower turns its head towards the sun and grows in garden beds.

clue.text: Fragrant mixture of grass for French king-emperor

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
pour is the French for 'for'
RI stands for Rex Imperator, the Latin title king and emperor

explanation.surface: A scented blend of herbs is prepared for a French monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-pourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for its scent.

clue.text: Youth qualified as overseer in a furniture shop?

definitions.text: Youth qualified as overseer in a furniture shop?

parts.words: Youth qualified as overseer in a furniture shop?
parts.note: a youth described by a word for height, the piece that overlooks the rest in a furniture showroom

explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a high chest of drawers, standing above the other furniture.

clue.text: Climber's sort of point d'appui

parts.note: a point d'appui is a fixed point of support; a mountaineer's version is a metal spike driven into rock

explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a peg hammered into a crack to anchor a climbing rope, literally a point of support.

clue.text: Uncle Arly sat "Close beside a leafy —"

definitions.text: Uncle Arly sat "Close beside a leafy —"

parts.words: Uncle Arly sat "Close beside a leafy —"
parts.note: a line from Edward Lear's poem Incidents in the Life of my Uncle Arly, with its last word left blank

explanation.definitionFit: Lear's line ends with a dense growth of shrubs, a leafy copse.

clue.text: Her speech abnormal — a proper part to play

definitions.text: Her speech abnormal — a proper part to play

indicators.note: only part of the words abnormal and proper is used, the letters running across the dash

explanation.surface: A stage role for a woman whose speech is oddly 'proper'.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'abnorMAL — A PROPer', marked by 'part'; the whole clue describes Mrs Malaprop of Sheridan's The Rivals, famed for misused words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Malaprop is a comic role in Sheridan's play The Rivals whose grand misused words gave us malapropism.

clue.text: Entertainment barred ?

parts.note: an entertainment written out in bars on a stave, though 'barred' suggests forbidden

explanation.definitionFit: Music is a form of entertainment and is notated in bars.

clue.text: An ape's wild song of triumph

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A monkey bursts into a raucous victory chant.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a hymn of praise or thanksgiving, especially for victory.

clue.text: Old character one found in a foreign state

parts.note: un is the French for 'a'

indicators.note: the word one is placed inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is a short form of California, a US state
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly eccentric is discovered living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter of a script, not a person; 'found in' puts I inside CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncial is a rounded capital script of early manuscripts, so an old form of letter.

clue.text: No bid — having no honours ?

definitions.meaning: in bridge, saying no bid means declining to bid
an ordinary university degree awarded without honours

explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a player declining to bid says this; an ordinary degree without honours is also called this.

clue.text: Smaller groups ordered into a green bus

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a new sequence, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Small parties are told to get into a green bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Subgenera are divisions in biological classification below a genus, smaller groupings of species.

clue.text: Oblique, like a Thames bridge

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
Kew Bridge crosses the Thames in west London

explanation.surface: A slanting structure resembling one of London's river crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is crooked or at a slant, not straight.

clue.text: Hot stuff in the outskirts of Kensington, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the letters are spoken, so their sound counts and not their spelling
the outskirts are the edges of a place, so we take the outside letters of the word Kensington

explanation.surface: Something spicy is reported on the edges of a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: KENSINGTON is a smart district of west London. Its first and last letters, said as letter names, sound like the pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a fiery red pepper, a hot spice.

clue.text: Jersey's Village Blacksmith for instance

definitions.meaning: a jersey is a knitted pullover
Longfellow's poem The Village Blacksmith says his brow is wet with honest sweat, so he is one who sweats

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the woollen garment; the other is a person who perspires, like Longfellow's toiling blacksmith.
